scenes.name: every step reads more than the last
scenes.visual: Dark stage. Top band header, white: 'Every new token re-reads the whole conversation'. Top-left, a small grey reference tag 'weights: 140 GB every step' that appears in b1 and then dims. Centre: a staircase of three rows of token pills, left-aligned, one row per decode step, each row one pill longer than the one above. Row 1: blue 't1' 't2' 't3' and an amber 't4'. Row 2: blue 't1'..'t4' and amber 't5'. Row 3: blue 't1'..'t5' and amber 't6'. Amber marks the token being computed in that step. At the right end of each row a grey tag: 'reads 4', 'reads 5', 'reads 6'. From each amber pill, thin coral arcs (coral = bytes read) reach back over every pill in its row, plus a small loop onto itself. A faint dotted diagonal traces the rising right edge. Bottom third, from b3: two cards, left amber with a circular-arrows icon 'recompute it', right teal with an archive-box icon 'keep it' holding a small stack. This staircase silhouette returns in scene 5, so keep its proportions. The idea the motion makes visible: each step reads more than the one before, and nothing carries over between steps by itself.

beats.say: Each decode step reads every weight. It also reads a second thing, and this one grows.
beats.show: On 'every weight', the grey tag 'weights: 140 GB every step' fades in top-left, then dims to 30%. On 'this one grows', the header writes on and a faint empty row guide appears in the centre.

beats.say: The newest token, lit up, attends over every token before it and itself: four, then five, then six. That staircase is the picture behind a cost growing with the square of the length.
beats.show: Row 1 slides in; on 'attends over', four coral arcs draw from t4 back to t1, t2, t3 and loop onto t4; on 'four', tag 'reads 4'. On 'five', row 2 builds directly below with five arcs and 'reads 5'; on 'six', row 3 with six arcs and 'reads 6'. On 'staircase', the dotted diagonal draws along the right edges. On 'square', the three rows pulse top to bottom and a grey key phrase fades in under them: 'each step longer than the last'.

beats.say: The model keeps no memory between steps. So its work on earlier tokens is either redone every time, or kept, in a store that grows. Which is cheaper?
beats.show: On 'no memory', rows 2 and 3 dim; row 1's arcs fade to nothing, a grey label 'nothing carried over' appears in the gap between rows 1 and 2, then row 2 re-brightens with all its arcs drawn fresh. On 'redone', the amber card 'recompute it' rises bottom-left, its arrows spinning. On 'kept', the teal card 'keep it' rises bottom-right; the staircase rows pulse once more top to bottom, and the card's small stack gains one block per pulse. On 'Which is cheaper?', a grey question mark appears between the two cards.

scenes.name: the causal triangle
scenes.visual: Opens on the 5 by 5 score grid from chapter 8, exactly as it was left: rows labelled 'the' 'cat' 'sat' 'down' 'it' with a magnifier icon, columns with the same words and a key icon. Those labels morph into 'token 1'.. 'token 5' down the left and a grey column note 'keys it may attend to'. Allowed cells, the lower-left triangle including the diagonal, light blue; forbidden cells, upper-right, dark grey with faint hatching and the label 'masked'. Header top band: 'Attention is causal', grey subline 'a token sees only what came before it'. From b3 the big grid slides into the left third and shrinks, and the right two-thirds hold two mini-grids side by side, 'Prefill' (left) and 'Decode' (right). Beside Decode, a small chip icon with idle grey cores, labelled 'not the hardware'. The idea the motion makes visible: the triangle fills all at once when every token exists, and one row at a time when each token must wait for the one before, with earlier rows never touched again.

beats.say: Bring back the grid of scores. Token one sees only itself. Token five sees all five.
beats.show: The chapter 8 grid fades in with word labels; on 'grid of scores', the labels morph to 'token 1'..'token 5' and the column note appears. On 'token one', only row 1's first cell lights blue; rows 2, 3 and 4 light two, three and four cells in quick succession; on 'all five', row 5 lights fully.

beats.say: Everything ahead is masked out: the causal mask. A token sees only what came before it, so only a triangle is used.
beats.show: On 'masked out', the upper-right cells fill dark grey with hatching, one diagonal band at a time, and 'masked' fades in over them. On 'causal mask', the header and subline write on. On 'triangle', a counter top right of the grid reads '15 / 25'; the cells then shrink into the fine mesh of a much larger square with the same lit triangle, the counter changes to '≈ half', and the grid returns to 5 by 5.

beats.say: You met the chain earlier: the next token cannot exist until the last is chosen. Under the mask, each new row only looks back, and never changes the rows above.
beats.show: Header subline fades. The big grid slides into the left third and shrinks. Right side: mini-grid 'Decode' draws empty and lights row 1. On 'cannot exist', an amber token pill drops out of row 1's right end, slides down with a small chain-link icon and becomes row 2's label; only then does row 2 light. On 'only looks back', row 2's lit cells glow under columns 1 and 2. On 'never changes', small teal padlocks settle on row 1's cells and stay.

beats.say: Prefill, with every token present, fills the triangle in one shot. Decode adds a row at a time, so each read of the weights serves one token.
beats.show: Mini-grid 'Prefill' appears left of Decode; on 'one shot', its whole triangle flashes blue at once, teal tag 'one shot'. On 'a row at a time', Decode ticks rows 3, 4 and 5 one by one, each new row padlocking the one above; amber tag 'one row at a time'. On 'serves one token', a small coral 'weights read' tile drops beside each Decode row as it lights, tagged '1 token'. The chip icon 'not the hardware' fades in beside Decode.

scenes.name: the redundant work, and two ways to grow
scenes.visual: Header top band: 'The observation that saves everything'. Left half, upper: a row of six blue token pills 't1' to 't6', each with a small blue key tile 'K' and value tile 'V' stacked above it; an amber pill 't7' arrives from the right. A teal-bordered banner over them, two lines: 'Earlier keys and values' / 'do not depend on the new token'. Left half, lower, from b2: a blue box 'generating token 1,000' and an amber box 'recompute 999 positions'; then a staircase of amber blocks in columns of 0, 1, 2 and 3 inside a dashed 4 by 3 rectangle, and an equation that builds term by term. Right half, from b4: one chart titled 'Two ways to grow', a single shared y axis 'total work' and x axis 'tokens', a teal straight line 'Linear' and an amber upward curve 'Quadratic', with a strip of per-token bars under each, and a grey 'schematic' tag. The idea the motion makes visible: earlier keys and values are frozen, so recomputing them is pure repetition, and that repetition piles up as a triangle whose total outruns anything linear.

beats.say: Now the observation that saves everything: earlier keys and values do not depend on the new token. Settled when their tokens were processed, they never change.
beats.show: Header writes on. Left upper: t1 to t6 with their K and V tiles. On 'the new token', t7 slides in amber from the right; the earlier tiles stay perfectly still and the teal banner draws on. On 'never change', a small query arrow from t3 tries to reach forward to t7 and stops at a thin grey wall labelled 'mask', with the grey label 't3 never saw t7'; arrow and wall fade, and small teal padlocks settle onto every earlier K and V tile.

beats.say: Recomputing them is identical work, repeated. Generating token one thousand would recompute all nine hundred and ninety-nine earlier positions.
beats.show: Upper group dims to 40%. On 'token one thousand', the blue box 'generating token 1,000' appears lower left; on 'nine hundred and ninety-nine', the amber box 'recompute 999 positions' appears beside it and a dense strip of 999 hairline amber ticks flashes beneath.

beats.say: Add it up: for n tokens, n times one less than n, then halved. For a thousand, about half a million recomputations, where a thousand would do.
beats.show: Boxes shrink upward. On 'Add it up', four columns of 0, 1, 2 and 3 amber blocks build left to right with '0 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 6'; a dashed 4 by 3 rectangle outlines them and its empty half shades grey: '4 × 3 = 12, half = 6'. On 'then halved', the equation morphs to 'total = n(n − 1) / 2', tag 'quadratic in n'. On 'a thousand', n becomes 1,000 and an amber counter runs to 499,500; a small teal '1,000' sits beside it.

beats.say: Two shapes worth recognising. Linear: flat work per token. Quadratic: each token costs more than the last. Barely different at ten tokens, at ten thousand quadratic is about a thousand times worse.
beats.show: Right half: the chart draws with its shared axes and grey 'schematic' tag. On 'Linear', equal teal bars fill the strip under the axis and the teal total climbs as a straight line. On 'Quadratic', the amber block columns from the left slide across into the strip as rising bars and the amber total bends upward. On 'ten tokens', both curves are marked at x = 10, 'about equal'. On 'ten thousand', the x axis stretches to 10,000 and the y axis visibly rescales: its tick labels jump, the teal line flattens toward the floor while the amber curve climbs. Tags: teal '× 1,000', amber '× 1,000,000', and an amber readout '≈ 1,000× worse'.

beats.say: Recomputing is the quadratic shape, so nobody does it: long conversations would be impossible, not merely expensive. Almost every scaling problem ahead is one such term outgrowing everything linear.
beats.show: A label 'recompute every step' attaches to the amber curve; on 'impossible', the curve runs off the top of the frame with the tag 'impossible, not just expensive'. Left half dims. On 'Almost every', a key phrase fades in under the chart: 'one quadratic term outgrows everything linear'.

scenes.name: what a cache is, in general
scenes.visual: Header top band, two lines: 'A cache is something kept' / 'so it need not be made again'. Two cards side by side in the centre. Left, amber: a calculator icon and 'work it out every time', with a small tally counter. Right, teal: a calculator icon, a sticky-note icon and 'work it out once, keep it'. Lower centre, from b2: a balance-scale icon with a coral block 'space' on one pan and a teal block 'time saved' on the other. In b3 the sticky note morphs into a vertical stack of thin teal entries that grows. The idea the motion makes visible: a cache spends space to save repeated effort, and pays only when the kept thing is used again.

beats.say: First the general idea; it makes the specific easier to judge. A cache is something kept so it need not be made again.
beats.show: The two cards fade up, still. On 'A cache is', the two-line header writes on.

beats.say: Work it out once, note it, then read the note. The trade is always memory for time, paying only if the note is read again.
beats.show: Left card shows '37 × 48'; its calculator pulses four times as the tally counts 1, 2, 3, 4. Right card: on 'once', the calculator pulses once and a sticky note appears, '37 × 48 = 1,776'; on 'read the note', it glows teal three times as later requests read it. On 'memory for time', the balance scale appears: coral 'space' drops onto one pan, teal 'time saved' rises on the other. On 'read again', a second note '52 × 17 = 884' appears, sits unread and fades to grey, tag 'never reused: wasted space'.

beats.say: In decode, every earlier token is needed at every later step, about as favourable as it gets. The cost: the store grows every token. That is the key-value cache.
beats.show: Grey note and scale fade. The useful note morphs into a vertical stack of thin teal entries. Each step one entry is added on top, and on every step all entries glow at once, showing that every one is used. On 'grows', a coral tag beside it: 'grows every token'. On 'key-value cache', the stack is labelled 'key-value cache', and a small grey tag appears under it: 'the central problem ahead'.

scenes.name: the key-value cache
scenes.visual: Left half: the GPU package illustration, compute die in the middle, HBM stacks around it, a wide bus between them. One HBM stack is enlarged; inside it a region outlined teal and labelled 'KV cache' holds rows of paired tiles, one row per token, each a small K tile and V tile. Right half, top: a panel 'Each decode step' with three boxes in a row joined by arrows: amber 'compute one K and V', teal 'append to cache', coral 'read the whole cache'. Right half, lower: a small counter area used in b3, then, in b4, the staircase silhouette from scene 1 (rows of pills with coral arcs and 'reads' tags). Coral particles always mean the cache being read. The idea the motion makes visible: each step creates one new entry, adds it to the end, and then reads everything that has accumulated, so the computing stops growing but the reading does not.

beats.say: The server's notes from earlier are exactly these: each token's keys and values, kept in a dedicated region of H B M.
beats.show: GPU package fades in. On 'notes', a grey sticky-note icon labelled 'the server's notes' appears over the package and splits into rows of K and V tile pairs. On 'H B M', the camera pushes into one HBM stack; the rows settle into a region that outlines teal and is labelled 'KV cache', six rows already in it.

beats.say: Each decode step now computes only the new token's key and value, appends them, and reads the whole cache for attention.
beats.show: Camera eases back so package and cache region are both visible; the panel 'Each decode step' draws on top right, unlit. On 'computes', the amber box lights and one K and V pair appears on the die. On 'appends', the pair slides along the bus into the next empty row and the teal box lights. On 'reads', coral particles stream from every row of the cache back to the die and the coral box lights.

beats.say: Nothing earlier is recomputed: the recomputing goes from quadratic to linear. Every serving system does this; it is why decode is practical at all.
beats.show: The three-box loop runs three more times, faster each time, the cache gaining a row per pass. Lower right: a teal counter 'K and V computed: 1,000' beside an amber '499,500' that is struck through; tag 'recompute: quadratic → linear'. On 'Every serving system', four small server-rack icons slide in along the bottom, each with a teal 'KV cache' badge, and a grey tag 'obvious once seen'.

beats.say: But every token still reads the whole cache. The staircase from the start is still there, each step reading a little more than the last.
beats.show: Racks and counters fade. On 'reads the whole cache', the coral box pulses and the coral read stream thickens as more rows accumulate. On 'staircase', the scene 1 staircase silhouette fades in lower right with its coral arcs; a fourth and fifth row add themselves in step with the cache's new rows. Coral tag: 'reads: still growing'.

beats.say: A caching trick that solves one problem, and creates the one that dominates everything downstream.
beats.show: The scene dims except the cache region and its coral stream. Key phrase centred: 'solves one problem, creates the next'.

scenes.name: what actually re-enters the model each step
scenes.visual: Two horizontal lanes on the left two-thirds; on the right, a model block drawn as a tall stack of thin layer slabs that both lanes feed. Top lane, header 'What you might picture', subline 'the whole text, fed in again': nine blue token pills and an ellipsis, label 'all 1,032 tokens, every step'. Bottom lane, header 'What actually happens', subline 'one token, plus the cache': nine dashed-outline pills, each with a tiny K and V tile, and one solid amber pill at the right end; label 'already in the cache, not recomputed'. Between the lanes, from b2: two bars drawn to scale. Teal threads from the amber pill back to the dashed pills mean reused, not recomputed. The idea the motion makes visible: the text grows, but only one token enters the model per step.

beats.say: One correction most people need. It is tempting to picture all one thousand and thirty-two tokens of the weather chat re-entering the model every step.
beats.show: Model block draws on the right. Top lane builds: nine blue pills, ellipsis, label 'all 1,032 tokens, every step'. A small step counter ticks 1, 2, 3; on each tick the whole row streams into the model block.

beats.say: That would be a thousand times the work at this length, and worse as it grows. Only the newest token goes through. The rest is already there, as keys and values.
beats.show: On 'a thousand times', two bars draw between the lanes to scale: amber '1,032 tokens per step', long; teal '1 token per step', a sliver; tag '≈ 1,000×'. On 'worse as it grows', the amber bar lengthens a little. On 'Only the newest', the bottom lane builds: dashed pills with their label, and only the amber pill flows into the model. On 'keys and values', teal threads reach back from it to each dashed pill, lighting its small K and V tile.

beats.say: The sequence grows, but the work per step does not grow with it the way that picture suggests.
beats.show: Top lane is crossed out, dims and slides off; bars fade. In the bottom lane, the amber pill turns dashed and joins the row, a new amber pill arrives and flows in alone: the row is longer, the flow into the model is still one pill. Key phrase where the top lane was: 'one token in, plus the cache'.

scenes.name: where the eighty comes from
scenes.visual: Top band: an equation in a bar with a thin white outline, set on two lines: 'cache per token =' / '2 × layers × KV heads × head dim × bytes'. Terms land one at a time, each with a small grey label beneath. In this scene only '2' and '× layers' land; the rest are blank slots. Lower left: the tempting picture from chapter 8, an 'embedding' box with a single block of three tiles 'Q', 'K', 'V' above it and one arrow carrying it up a stack of layers. Lower right: two stacks of eighty thin layer slabs side by side, the left one dimmer and labelled 'earlier token', the right one brighter and labelled 'new token'; every slab holds its own small K and V tile pair. The idea the motion makes visible: the layers term exists only because every layer makes and keeps its own key and value.

beats.say: How big is the cache? Build its formula for one token: two, one key and one value, then the layers.
beats.show: 'cache per token =' writes on, with blank slots after it. On 'two', '2' lands with a blue K tile and V tile beneath and the grey label 'one key, one value'. On 'layers', '× layers' lands, grey label 'layers'.

beats.say: In the tempting picture from earlier, query, key and value are made once and carried up: no layers term. But every layer makes its own, from its own input and weights.
beats.show: Lower left, the tempting picture redraws: 'embedding', the one Q, K, V block, one arrow up the stack. On 'no layers term', a teal tag 'no layers term' appears under it and '× layers' in the equation flickers grey. On 'every layer makes its own', the tempting picture is crossed out and dims; lower right, the two stacks of eighty slabs draw upward, each slab growing its own K and V pair in a slightly different shade of blue. Tag '× 80'.

beats.say: And all eighty are kept: layer forty needs an earlier token's layer-forty key, not its layer-one key. Made once, the cache would be eighty times smaller, and most of this series would not exist.
beats.show: On 'layer forty', a query arrow runs from the new token's slab 40 straight across to the earlier token's slab-40 K tile, which lights. The earlier stack's slab-1 K tile greys out with a small cross and the label 'wrong layer'. On 'eighty times smaller', '× layers' glows coral and gains the value '80' beneath, and a grey ghost of one stack collapses to a single slab, tag '÷ 80'. Key phrase lower centre: 'every layer keeps its own'.

scenes.name: three hundred and twenty kilobytes per token
scenes.visual: Top band: the two-line equation from scene 7 persists; its remaining slots fill with numbers as they are spoken. Left third: one blue token pill at the bottom; above it a tall column of eighty slots labelled 'L1', 'L2', … 'L10', '…', 'L80', each slot a small K and V pair; header over the column 'One token, eighty layers deep'. Right two-thirds: an arithmetic panel that builds per-layer bytes, then the per-token total, with a coral byte counter. The idea the motion makes visible: a small per-layer amount, multiplied by eighty.

beats.say: The rest is the model's shape, Llama three seventy B: eight key-value heads, each a hundred and twenty-eight numbers wide, two bytes per number.
beats.show: A grey tag 'Llama 3 70B' appears beside the equation. On 'eight', '× KV heads' lands with '8' under it; on 'a hundred and twenty-eight', '× head dim' lands with '128'; on 'two bytes', '× bytes' lands with '2' and the grey label '16-bit'. Right panel: a K tile stretches into eight segments of 128 cells, label '8 × 128 = 1,024 numbers', and a matching V tile beside it.

beats.say: Two, times eight, times a hundred and twenty-eight, times two: four thousand and ninety-six bytes, about four kilobytes per layer. Times eighty: three hundred and twenty-seven thousand, six hundred and eighty bytes.
beats.show: Right panel builds '2 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 4,096 bytes' one term per spoken number, then the label 'per layer, per token: 4 KB'; slot 'L1' fills with its pair. On 'Times eighty', slots L2 to L80 fill rapidly and a coral counter runs to 327,680. The top equation becomes fully numeric: '2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2 = 327,680 bytes'.

beats.say: About three hundred and twenty kilobytes per token. It is large because of the eighty: every layer holds its own version of the token.
beats.show: Large figure centre right: '≈ 320 KB per token', with a small grey note under it '327,680 bytes = 320 × 1,024' and a grey tag 'used from here on'. On 'the eighty', the '80' term and the whole left column glow coral together; label beside the column: 'a key and a value at every one of the eighty'.

scenes.name: which terms can shrink
scenes.visual: Top band: the numeric equation '2 × 80 × 8 × 128 × 2' with each term labelled underneath: 'K and V', 'layers', 'KV heads', 'head dim', 'bytes'. Centre: two horizontal coral bars drawn to scale: a long ghost bar '64 KV heads: 2.6 MB per token' and a bar one-eighth as long '8 KV heads: 320 KB per token'. Lower band: a padlock on the layers term and three teal arrows pointing up at the shrinkable terms. The idea the motion makes visible: the eighty cannot move, so every saving has to come from the other terms.

beats.say: Here the shared key-value heads from earlier pay off. Sixty-four, one per query head, would make the cache eight times bigger: about two point six megabytes per token.
beats.show: In the equation, the '8' under 'KV heads' turns into '64' and glows amber. On 'eight times bigger', a long coral ghost bar draws across the centre, label '64 KV heads: 2.6 MB per token', with a small grey '× 8' at its end.

beats.say: That eightfold cut is grouped-query attention, already built in. Nothing cuts the layers, because the layers are the model.
beats.show: The '64' turns back to '8', now teal. The ghost bar contracts to one-eighth of its length, '8 KV heads: 320 KB per token', with a teal tag 'grouped-query attention: ÷ 8'. On 'Nothing cuts the layers', a padlock settles onto the '80', label 'that is the model'.

beats.say: So every technique that shrinks the cache attacks another term: fewer heads, narrower heads, or fewer bytes per number. Knowing which makes the rest of the series easier to follow.
beats.show: Three teal arrows draw up from below, one per phrase: 'fewer heads' to 'KV heads', 'narrower heads' to 'head dim', 'fewer bytes' to 'bytes'. On 'Knowing which', the bars fade and the labelled equation sits alone in the centre, with '320 KB, decomposed' beneath it.

scenes.name: how big the cache gets
scenes.visual: Upper band: a blue bar, full width minus margins, labelled 'weights: 140 GB', fixed as the reference. Under it, drawn to the same scale, a coral bar 'KV cache' that starts at zero length and grows. Grey note 'drawn to scale'. Left: a token counter. Right third: a three-row table that fills: '1,000 tokens → 0.33 GB', '10,000 tokens → 3.3 GB', '100,000 tokens → 33 GB'. Both bars stay on screen into the next scene. The idea the motion makes visible: the cache grows in a straight line with the conversation, and at long lengths it is a sizeable fraction of the model itself.

beats.say: The cache grows in a straight line with the conversation. A thousand tokens: a third of a gigabyte.
beats.show: Weights bar draws on, '140 GB'; empty coral cache bar beneath, counter at '0 tokens'. On 'A thousand', the counter runs to 1,000, the cache bar becomes a hairline, and the row '1,000 tokens → 0.33 GB' appears. Without narration, the counter runs on to 10,000, the bar becomes a thin sliver, row '10,000 tokens → 3.3 GB'.

beats.say: A hundred thousand: thirty-three gigabytes, already a quarter of the model itself, for one conversation.
beats.show: On 'A hundred thousand', the counter runs to 100,000, the cache bar reaches about a quarter of the weights bar, row '100,000 tokens → 33 GB'. On 'a quarter', a bracket joins the 33 GB bar to the 140 GB bar, tag '≈ ¼ of the model'; small grey tag 'one conversation'.

beats.say: A formula worth memorising: it turns any model's shape and context length straight into gigabytes.
beats.show: The two-line equation returns in the top band. Two input tags slide into it from the left, 'any model shape' and 'any context length'; an output tag appears on the right: 'gigabytes'.

scenes.name: the cache and the weights compete
scenes.visual: Continues from scene 10's two bars, which fold into blocks. GPU package across the frame, compute die on the right. On the left, a large rounded panel 'HBM, one bandwidth budget' containing two blocks: a wide blue one 'weights, read every step' and a narrower one 'cache, read every step' that can grow. A single bus runs from the panel to the die, carrying coral particles from both blocks; grey label under the bus 'both draw on the same bus'. Top right: a ceiling readout 'tokens/s ≤ bandwidth ÷ bytes per token' with live numbers. Later, five small cache blocks sit beside the weights block, and four teal technique cards slide up along the bottom. Keep at most five text items visible: labels fade as new ones arrive. The idea the motion makes visible: the weights and the cache drain one shared pipe, so a bigger cache means fewer tokens per second.

beats.say: Every step reads every weight and every cache entry so far, over one bus. So the ceiling from earlier, bandwidth over bytes per token, sinks as the cache grows.
beats.show: The two bars fold into blocks inside the HBM panel; the bus and die draw on. On 'every weight', coral particles flow from the weights block along the bus; on 'every cache entry', particles from the cache block join the same bus; label 'both draw on the same bus'. On 'the ceiling', the readout builds top right: 'tokens/s ≤ bandwidth ÷ bytes per token'.

beats.say: On an H one hundred, the weights alone allow about twenty-four tokens a second. Add a hundred-thousand-token cache, and each step reads a hundred and seventy-three gigabytes: about nineteen. Illustrative, but the direction is general.
beats.show: Readout fills: '3.35 TB/s ÷ 140 GB ≈ 24 tokens/s'. On 'a hundred-thousand-token cache', the cache block grows to '33 GB'; the denominator becomes '140 + 33 = 173 GB' and the result counter drops from 24 to 19, the particle stream per token visibly longer. Grey tag 'illustrative: one request, H100'. On 'general', a small slider beside the readout: as the cache block grows the number falls, as it shrinks the number rises.

beats.say: Batching shares one read of the weights among many conversations, but each cache is read for its own conversation alone.
beats.show: Slider, illustrative tag, readout and bus label fade; the block labels shorten to 'weights' and 'cache'. On 'shares one read', the weights block gains a teal tag 'read once, shared', and five small user icons appear beside the die, one particle stream from the weights block branching to all five. On 'each cache', five small cache blocks appear in shades of coral under one bracket 'one cache per conversation', each streaming to its own user icon only.

beats.say: That competition shapes every technique ahead: shrinking the cache, sharing it between requests that start alike, splitting it across machines, or never storing parts at all.
beats.show: The bracket fades. Four teal cards slide up along the bottom, one per phrase: a shrink-arrows icon 'shrink it'; a two-users icon 'share a common prefix'; a two-servers icon 'split across machines'; a crossed-out-block icon 'don't store parts'.

beats.say: The model and the conversation's state: two different things, reading from one budget. Once the cache is large, optimising the weights alone stops being enough.
beats.show: Cards dim. On 'two different things', the weights block and the cache blocks pulse in turn. Key phrase centred over the panel: 'two things, one budget'.

checks.claim: fig 132 (on screen): with 5 tokens the causal triangle uses 1+2+3+4+5 = 15 of 25 cells
fig 132 (on screen): with 1,000 tokens the triangle is almost exactly half the grid
fig 133 (on screen): four-token example 0 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 = 4 x 3 / 2 (half of a 4 by 3 rectangle)
fig 133: for 1,000 tokens, n(n-1)/2 = 499,500 position recomputations, about half a million

fig 134: if linear and quadratic totals are about equal at 10 tokens, going to 10,000 grows linear x1,000 and quadratic about x1,000,000, so quadratic ends about 1,000 times worse. Atlas wording 'a thousand times worse' is read as this ratio; with n(n-1)/2 the exact figure is 1,111, hence 'about'
